newsitem.title: HONG KONG: PRESS DIGEST - HK Newspaper Editorials - June 26.
newsitem.headline: PRESS DIGEST - HK Newspaper Editorials - June 26.

text.p: There are five days to go before the British colony reverts to China. These are highlights of comments in the Hong Kong press. The views expressed are those of the newspapers quoted and do not represent an editorial viewpoint of Reuters.

-- The ECONOMIC TIMES said the decision by the U.S. and British governments to send officals to attend the swearing-in of the provisional legislature showed that their attempt to unite western countries to boycott the body had completely failed. It said the change of attitude was embarrassing and made the two governments look stupid. The paper said the episode proved that international politics was all about interests, and London and Washington's previous decisions failed because they were against the interests of their people.

-- The English-language SOUTH CHINA MORNING POST said after weeks of portraying themselves as taking a highly principled stance in announcing their leaders would boycott the swearing-in of the provisional legislature, the announcement by Britain and the United States that they would be sending representatives had invited scorn. Their attempt to "have their cake and eat it" meant that London and Washington had forfeited any right to the moral high ground which they liked to claim. They opted for shilly-shallying edging towards hypocrisy, the paper said.

-- The Beijing-backed WEN WEI PO said the decision of the U.S. Congress to renew China's Most Favoured Nation (MFN) trade status came as expected, because all countries' policies now revolved around economic interests. It said if the Americans wanted to explore the mainland market, their government had to be more friendly with China. The paper said if the United States refused to renew China's MFN trade status, it would isolate itself internationally before isolating China.
